test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In which soil does cotton grow best?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Black soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Black soil is also known as **Regur soil** and is ideal for growing cotton.
 
• It is **rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime**, which are essential nutrients for cotton growth.
 
• Black soil has a high moisture-retaining capacity, making it suitable for cotton farming.
 
• This soil is predominantly found in the **Deccan Plateau** region, covering parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brown Soil**

 
 
• Brown soil is a type of **loam soil** that is typically fertile and suitable for growing various crops.
 
• It is well-draining and rich in organic matter but not particularly suitable for cotton cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil**
 
 
• Red soil is rich in **iron oxide** which gives it a reddish color.
 
• It is commonly found in parts of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh but is less suitable for cotton due to its lower nutrient content and poor moisture retention.
 
 
 
• **Yellow Soil**
 
 
• Yellow soil is formed by the weathering of ancient crystalline rocks and is found in parts of Orissa and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is less fertile compared to black soil and not ideal for cotton cultivation.
